constitutive_assumptions: Constant curvature deformation along the actuator length in both activated and non-activated jamming states
Incompressibility of the silicone elastomer (product of principal deformation ratios equals one)
Fiber reinforcement prevents radial expansion, constraining the radial deformation ratio to one
Euler-Bernoulli beam theory applies to the layer jamming packet, acting as a single unified beam without slip under small deflections during the activated state
Strain energy contribution of the layer jamming structure is negligible in the nonactive (unpressurized) phase
Gravitational effects are negligible due to horizontal actuation supported by a low-friction surface perpendicular to gravity
Quasi-static conditions assume frequency-dependent dynamic damping effects are minimal at low actuation frequencies
control_variables: Inner diameter of the semicylindrical section (6.35 mm)
Wall thickness of the semicylindrical section (3 mm)
Flat base thickness of the actuator (3.4 mm)
Number of paper layers in the layer jamming packet (25 layers)
Thickness of each paper layer (0.1 mm)
Horizontal testing plane on a low-friction support plate perpendicular to gravity
dependent_variables: Bending angle (angular deflection) of the actuator
Residual bending angle after pressure depletion
Prediction error between modeled and experimental bending angles

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Integrating a layer jamming packet into a soft bending actuator increases structural stiffness by more than nine times when vacuum is activated.
The activated actuator exhibits linear bending behavior up to approximately 0.8 bar, beyond which interlayer shear overcomes static friction and initiates layer slip and nonlinear behavior.

An analytical strain energy model based on Neo-Hookean hyperelasticity and Euler-Bernoulli beam theory predicts linear bending behavior with a 6.3% average error but fails to capture post-slip nonlinear response.

A modified Prandtl-Ishlinskii hysteresis model incorporating an exponential growth term captures asymmetric multi-loop saturated hysteresis across both linear and nonlinear regimes with approximately 8.5% error.
Pressure depletion following actuation beyond the linear threshold results in an unrecovered residual bending angle that can be quantitatively predicted from layer slip mechanics.
The modified Prandtl-Ishlinskii model maintains accuracy (approximately 8% error) when tested at twice the identification frequency within the quasi-static regime.

experimental_setup: Molded RTV2-325 (Shore A) liquid silicone soft bending actuator with intersecting helical reinforcement fibers and an inextensible bottom strap
Layer jamming packet containing 25 sheets of 100-micrometer-thick paper enclosed in a heat-sealed polyethylene sleeve and encased with the soft bending actuator in elastic fabric
Air compressor providing positive inflation pressure to the soft bending actuator
Festo MPYE-5-1/8-HF-010B proportional solenoid valve regulating positive input pressure
Value VE280N vacuum pump providing negative pressure to activate the layer jamming mechanism
National Instruments PCI-6052E 16-bit DAQ card controlling the valve and logging voltage from the sensor circuit
Flex Sensor 4.5 variable-resistance bending sensor in a voltage divider circuit calibrated via image processing and polynomial fitting
Low-friction horizontal support plate orienting actuator bending perpendicular to gravity
future_work: Extending the modeling framework to dynamic operating conditions
Determining the upper frequency limits of the proposed quasi-static hysteresis model
Comparing accuracy between the proposed model and dynamic models across varying actuation frequencies
independent_variables: Positive pneumatic actuation pressure applied to the soft bending actuator
Layer jamming state (active vacuum vs. inactive atmospheric pressure)
Number of repeated inflation-deflation actuation cycles
Input signal frequency (quasi-static ramp, low-frequency cyclic, doubled frequency)
limitations_inferred: The constant curvature assumption may break down under point contact loads, external grasping disturbances, or non-uniform localized layer slipping
The paper does not quantify grasping force generation or payload capacity against external objects
The nonlinear hysteresis model relies on empirical least-squares parameter optimization rather than a purely predictive first-principles tribological model
Long-term cyclic endurance, wear of the paper layers, and fatigue of the polyethylene vacuum packaging were not evaluated
Experimental evaluation was restricted to planar horizontal bending, leaving multi-axis deflection, twisting, and 3D gravitational loading unaddressed
limitations_stated_by_authors: The strain energy-based analytical method cannot accurately characterize the actuator's behavior in the nonlinear region or at high input pressures
Standard Prandtl-Ishlinskii models fail to capture the upward-shifting drift of consecutive hysteresis loops without adding a specialized growth compensation term
Operating frequencies exceeding the quasi-static range introduce frequency-dependent damping hysteresis that leads to a noticeable decline in model accuracy
Deflation leaves a permanent residual bending angle because the actuator's elastic recovery force is insufficient to overcome inter-layer friction after slipping
Exceeding a specific vacuum degassing duration during silicone casting makes the material excessively stiff
main_results: Activating the 25-sheet layer jamming mechanism increased the actuator stiffness by more than 9 times compared to the nonactive state
The system exhibits a linear response threshold up to roughly 0.8 bar, after which shear-induced inter-layer slippage causes a significant reduction in stiffness and produces nonlinear hysteresis
The linear strain energy model (Neo-Hookean + Euler-Bernoulli) achieved a 6.3% average prediction error in the linear regime but was unable to predict large-deformation nonlinear behavior

The modified Prandtl-Ishlinskii model with an exponential saturation term captured asymmetric, multi-cycle saturated hysteresis with an average error of approximately 8.5% across both linear and nonlinear regimes
Model validation at twice the identification frequency confirmed consistency within the quasi-static envelope with approximately 8% error

A predictable residual bending angle occurs upon deflation from pressures exceeding 0.8 bar due to friction between slipped layers, with theoretical predictions agreeing with experimental measurements within 3.1% to 9% error
modeling_methods: Strain energy method combining Neo-Hookean hyperelastic strain energy for the silicone actuator and Euler-Bernoulli beam strain energy for the layer jamming packet
Taylor series expansion to approximate deformation invariant terms
Castigliano's first theorem to derive the pressure-bending angle governing equilibrium equation
Modified Prandtl-Ishlinskii (PI) model combining rate-independent backlash operators, multi-condition saturation functions, and an exponential cycle-dependent growth term for saturated hysteresis
Least-squares optimization for identifying hysteresis model parameters
performance_metrics: Stiffness enhancement ratio (greater than 9-fold increase upon activation)
Strain energy model prediction error in the linear range (6.3% average error)
Modified Prandtl-Ishlinskii model prediction error (8.5% average error during identification; approximately 8% at doubled frequency)
Maximum input pressure tested (up to 1.57 bar) and corresponding bending angles
Residual deformation angle (ranging from 3.6 degrees at 1.0 bar to 14 degrees at 1.57 bar)
Sensor measurement accuracy (within 0.1 degrees) and DAQ nominal angular resolution (approximately 0.005 degrees)
possible_gap_implications: Developing combined analytical and modified hysteresis models provides a basis for more accurate open-loop and closed-loop position control of variable-stiffness soft actuators in the presence of layer slip

Predicting residual angle accumulation addresses a key challenge in cyclic path planning, though mechanical or control reset methods may be needed to overcome permanent deformation in practical grasping tasks
The inability of the model to handle dynamic damping at higher frequencies highlights an unresolved need for comprehensive dynamic modeling frameworks for layer-jammed soft robots
paper.research_objective: To design, fabricate, and model a variable-stiffness soft pneumatic bending actuator integrated with a layer jamming mechanism, capturing both its linear response via hyperelastic strain energy theory and its nonlinear saturated hysteresis behavior via an extended Prandtl-Ishlinskii model, and validating the models experimentally.
paper.research_problem: Soft bending actuators suffer from inherently low stiffness and excessive deformation when subjected to opposing external forces, limiting their utility in grasping tasks; furthermore, existing literature lacks comprehensive motion and nonlinear saturated hysteresis modeling for soft actuators coupled with layer jamming mechanisms.
paper.robot_type: layer jamming soft pneumatic bending actuator
paper.title: Analysis and modeling of nonlinear saturated behavior of layer jamming soft pneumatic bending actuator
